_help: Universal multi-peer collaboration protocol config. Single source of truth. All peers read this. No hardcoding.

leader_election._human_interface_peer_note: Pinned terminal = cc (encoding-safe Edit/Write tooling). Identity is honored only if its health/statusline was observed within human_interface_peer_freshness_minutes; a stale terminal identity is a separate failure class (re-elect if stale). Rationale: incident 2026-07-07 where cx.standard (low tier) as terminal wrote docs and corrupted UTF-8 -> '?'.

role_enforcement.note: Direct peer file writes are policy-governed until filesystem hooks/locks enforce them.

deep_review.purpose: High-tier review when additional context is justified.

leader_election.reelect_per_task_note: If true, hub.py triggers elect-leader before every ask. Default false (session-scoped).

collab_rate._note: R:10 enforcement is hardcoded in hub.py. Dead config fields have been deprecated.

health._note_thresholds: These measure per-peer active context jsonl size, distinct from global autonomous_maintenance limits.

user_communication.note: Any peer may communicate directly with the Human. No fixed coordinator. Domain expertise guides who leads.

governed_file_manifest._doc: Machine-readable governed-file set for the LL-20260703-005 mutation guard (hub.py _governed_files). Paths are repo-root-relative. Files here are hashed before/after every peer ask; a change during a peer execution window (not allow_governed_mutation) logs GOVERNED_MUTATION_VIOLATION.

communication_policy._note_large_content: handoff uses HANDOFF_MAX_* truncation instead of file_ref
communication_policy._note_pty_chunk_telemetry: Added 2026-07-12 (T23, cc.fable-ratified permanent telemetry): _ask_with_pty emits one aggregate 'pty_chunk_arrival' routing_metrics.jsonl event per PTY ask, recording read/dequeue timestamps and byte counts for up to pty_chunk_telemetry_max_chunks reads (full min/p50/p95/max gap and queue-delay stats are always computed over ALL chunks regardless of truncation). This is the load-bearing measurement for distinguishing real CPU/priority throttling of a backgrounded process tree (steady, evenly-paced reads) from PTY-reader-thread/ConPTY-backpressure starvation (bursty reads - many chunks dequeued at once after a long gap) - see peer-characteristics.jsonl's PC-20260712-agent-backgrounding-degrades-long-asks. Purely additive observability; does not change any read/dequeue timing or the zombie-timeout/heartbeat mechanisms.
communication_policy._note_oversized_ask_guard: NOT a universal content cap - peer comms remain UNLIMITED in time and content per _note_zombie_profile_map. Oversized asks are not a universal content cap. For peers with known silent batch-then-dump behavior under complex tool use (currently proxied by requires_pty=true, i.e. ag), hub.py injects an incremental-progress instruction into the query before dispatch so the peer emits output within the zombie window, rather than hard-rejecting - confirmed necessary and effective by direct A/B measurement 2026-07-12: the same 7-item task failed silently at 752s unmodified, succeeded at 352s with the injected instruction. Other peers only receive warning telemetry (oversized_ask_detected), no query mutation. --force-tier0 bypasses the query transformation entirely and proceeds with the query unmodified, accepting the silent-batch risk explicitly. The zombie window (_note_zombie_profile_map) remains the only kill threshold. Root cause history: 2026-07-11 (ag+cx unanimous) corrected an earlier global hard-reject (hasty generalization of an ag-specific bug into a universal policy) to a requires_pty-scoped hard-reject; 2026-07-12 (user-prompted recheck, ag+cx+cc.fable) found the hard-reject itself was treating a real-but-mitigable characteristic (silent batch-then-dump, not actual output loss) as permanently fatal, and replaced it with the progress-injection mitigation - the hard-reject code path remains supported in _guard_oversized_ask but is no longer invoked from the production ask path. requires_pty is a stopgap proxy (transport detail, not a real capability flag); a purpose-built flag (e.g. flushes_partial_output) would be architecturally cleaner if more peers are added. Recursive ContextGate failover and runtime escalation do not re-check context-inflated prompts (guarded by _depth==0 and _escalation_depth==0); the check itself runs after peer/node resolution so it can read the target peer's requires_pty.
communication_policy._note_zombie_profile_map: Silence (no-output) window per profile. Peer comms are UNLIMITED in total time and content - ANY output chunk resets this clock, so a peer that keeps streaming is never killed. The same window applies from process start and after every output chunk; there is no separate startup fast-fail window (retired 2026-07-11: a shorter profile-scoped startup_profile_map killed 3 real cx calls at 180s while the peer was still legitimately working). A non-lethal peer_silent_startup warning is emitted once when initial silence crosses silent_startup_warning_sec - telemetry only, never kills. The zombie window is the only silence-based kill threshold. deepthink=900s (15m): streaming reasoning models never idle that long mid-work, so 15m of silence = hung.

model_profiles.note: Only root peers are tracked. Runtime normalization expands nested profiles into deterministic peer.profile nodes.

generated_artifacts.policy: Generated launcher outputs are tracked separately from governed source files and must not block consensus unless their generator, stable wrapper, or runtime behavior is affected.
generated_artifacts.audit_action: Classify volatile generated drift as informational; review the source of truth and stable wrapper before proposing source edits.

decision_tier_floor._terminal_file_write_note: A peer acting as terminal (human_interface_peer) MUST be at >= effort tier to perform direct file writes/edits. A *.standard / low-tier terminal is a thin router only: it routes, reviews, and delegates edits to an effort+ peer that applies them via encoding-safe Write. Enforces the thin-router rule (PRO-19). Incident 2026-07-07: cx.standard low-tier terminal corrupted UTF-8 docs.
decision_tier_floor.tier_floor_fallback: if a required voter's minimum-tier profile is rate-gated or unavailable, the vote MAY be cast at that peer's highest currently-available tier; the caveat MUST be recorded in the consensus record; any peer or the human may demand re-ratification at min-tier once available; offline abstain rules unchanged.

operational_guard.semi_governed_rule: Exempt only when current coordinator or role holder is RED, STALE, rate-limited, or missing (emergency recovery). Normal elective changes require visible proposal and peer verification. All semi-governed changes must write an audit record.

record_handoff.note: Part of consensus connector; governed under consensus finalize rules

consensus_finalize.note: Performs transition to finalized state and commits to handoff.md

autonomous_maintenance._doc: Phase 1 of self-evolution.md: declarative schedule for self_care.py and lifecycle scripts. IMPORTANT (clarified 2026-07-17, 3-peer closure review): despite the name, this is NOT a wall-clock/cron scheduler -- there is no background dispatcher that fires on a timer. 'enabled' means self_care.py fires at the ctx_start.py/ctx_end.py lifecycle HOOK POINTS (session_start/session_end), which only run when a human/wrapper actually invokes ctx-start.bat/ctx-end.bat. If those scripts are never run, self-care never fires, regardless of 'enabled'. Treat as manual-trigger-at-a-named-hookpoint, not autonomous-on-a-timer.

health_thresholds._note_health: These measure total system maintenance/log sizes, distinct from per-peer active context limits.
